title: Follow an event through local logs
goal: Correlate a journal event with a correctly scoped local rsyslog rule.
challenge: Send a bounded local5.notice event, find it in the journal, diagnose why the dedicated events.log rule misses it, validate and repair the rule, then prove a new event reaches both local destinations. Keep networking and forwarding disabled.

steps.command: logger -t ll-admin -p local5.notice "LAB_EVENT before"; sudo journalctl -t ll-admin -n 5 --no-pager; sudo cat /etc/rsyslog.d/40-learning-lab.conf
steps.explanation: logger uses the guest local Unix logging socket. Compare facility local5 with the existing selector.
steps.expected: The journal contains the event; the rule incorrectly selects local6.

steps.explanation: Change only local6.notice to local5.notice. Traditional .notice selects notice and more severe priorities; it is not exact-priority equality.
steps.expected: A local file action; no hostnames, @ forwarding or TCP/UDP input.

steps.command: sudo rsyslogd -N1 && sudo systemctl restart rsyslog.service
steps.explanation: Syntax validation must succeed before restart. This changes only the fresh guest logging service.

steps.command: logger -t ll-admin -p local5.notice "LAB_EVENT after"; sleep 1; sudo journalctl -t ll-admin -p notice -n 5 --no-pager; sudo cat /var/log/learning-lab/events.log
steps.explanation: Correlate the new message, tag and time. journalctl -p notice also includes more severe messages unless given an explicit range.
steps.expected: LAB_EVENT after appears in both local destinations.

steps.explanation: Keep the few-line evidence file; do not generate a logging flood.
steps.expected: A small root-owned protected log, normally root:adm 0640.

hints: The journal and rsyslog can both receive an event but apply different storage/filter policies.
Match the facility before changing the file path.
Test with a new marker after validation/restart; an old file can contain stale evidence.
review: I explained facility, severity and local action.
I validated the rule and correlated a new event without network logging.
coverage: Partial LPIC-1 108.2 local rsyslog and journal (partial). Guest-only administration; completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
